extracted.intended_audience: readers of ProPublica and other news consumers seeking corrections; journalists/editors tracking factual fixes
extracted.subtask_description: A corrections log for previously published news stories that records the original error, the correct information, and (when applicable) notes that the story or accompanying media were updated. Serves as a public record of factual and editorial corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact method for corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: To contact us with corrections, email us at [email protected].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers are instructed to submit corrections via the provided email address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard correction phrasing and dating
rubrics_metrics.description: Each item is labeled 'Correction, [date]:' and describes what the story originally said and what is correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections explicitly state the original misstatement and the accurate information, and they include the date the correction was issued (example: 'Correction, April 14, 2026: This story originally incorrectly reported the month ...').

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting misstated dates/times
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix errors about months, years, or timing in stories (e.g., an official arrived in January, not December; Janet Woodcock retired in 2024, not 2004).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the corrected date/time and clarify what was misstated in the original story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting mislabeled charts/data timestamps
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix chart or data-label errors, including incorrect dates associated with dataset snapshots (e.g., charts showed data as of December 2025, not Feb. 23, 2026).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update the chart labels and note the corrected data timestamp; explicitly state what the original label said and what has been fixed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting mischaracterization of companies' statements or statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend statements that misrepresent how a company characterized wages, ownership, or other claims (e.g., Nike did not say most workers earn double the minimum wage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify the company's actual formulation or data and remove or revise overstated language from the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting definitional or technical errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Correct inaccurate descriptions of technical terms or definitions in reporting (e.g., the definition of ectopic pregnancies; what counts as an ectopic pregnancy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace the inaccurate definition with the correct one and note the original error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting misidentified people (names, ages, nationalities, occupations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix errors in people's names, ages, nationalities, prior occupations, or titles (e.g., misidentified Jack Townsend's previous occupation; misspelled names; wrong ages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the correct identification and, where relevant, correct spellings and affiliations; examples on the page show corrections for spelling, nationality, age, and prior job titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting misattributed or misstated quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend quotes that were misquoted or misattributed (e.g., a White House spokesperson's words were corrected from 'America is safer without them' to 'America is safer with them out of our country').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reproduce the accurate quotation and note the misquote in the original reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting geographic or location errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix incorrect locations, hometowns, county/municipality associations, or headquarters (e.g., company headquartered in Farmers Branch, Texas, not Dallas).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the accurate place and correct any misleading geographic statements in the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting numerical/figure errors and estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend incorrect numerical claims, such as economic estimates, counts, or project values (e.g., $149 billion instead of $195 billion; number served by a nonprofit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the corrected numbers and clarify any contingent assumptions (example: an estimate was contingent on construction by a certain year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting misidentified institutions or agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix incorrect names of agencies, organizations, or institutional titles (e.g., Institute of Museum and Library Services vs. Institute for Museum and Library Services; FDIC vs. Federal Deposit Insurance Commission).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the proper institutional name and note the original misidentification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting photo/video caption and media identification errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend captions or video descriptions that misidentify people, places, or objects shown (e.g., misidentified a dam in a photograph; video misidentified a subject's teaching subject).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update captions/metadata for images and videos and note the correction in the log.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting legal or outcome misstatements
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix inaccurate descriptions of legal rulings, timelines, or the outcomes of lawsuits and cases (e.g., clarifying that a judge did not rule on whether there was abuse; dates between indictment and conviction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify the actual legal finding or timeline and correct the story language to avoid implying an incorrect legal outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting ownership/relationship assertions
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend unclear or incorrect claims about company ownership or the nature of relationships between entities (e.g., unclear if Harpeth Financial owns Action 247; shared executives/addresses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State what is publicly verifiable and remove unsupported ownership assertions; note when ownership is not made public or when clarity was lacking in original reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update the story and note when content has been changed
rubrics_metrics.description: When corrections require changing the article or its accompanying media, the correction note indicates that charts, photos, or the story text have been updated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly note in the correction that the story or media have been updated to reflect the correction (e.g., 'The charts have been updated to reflect the data as of Feb. 23, 2026').
